description: How TSMC's foundry surge left Intel behind — 2006–2026 market-cap race driven by smartphones, AI chips, supply shocks and the CHIPS-era boom.
youtube_description:
The Foundry Flip — a 20-year market-cap sprint where TSMC metamorphosed from one of many fabs into the world’s most valuable chipmaker, while Intel’s longtime dominance flattened under manufacturing struggles and strategic shifts. This chart-race traces the real events that reshaped silicon: the smartphone boom (2010s) that boosted contract fabs, TSMC’s aggressive node leadership, Intel’s delays on 10/7 nm, pandemic supply shocks and surging demand for AI accelerators, and policy responses like the U.S. CHIPS Act that rewired investment flows.

What you’ll see in this video:
- TSMC’s explosive climb as foundry customers (Apple, NVIDIA, AMD) outsourced advanced nodes.
- Intel’s market-cap slide during multi-year node delays and its pivot to IDM 2.0.
- Samsung’s roller-coaster as it battled memory cycles, foundry ambitions, and vertical integration.

Sources & accuracy: yearly company market-cap snapshots and major milestones (smartphone adoption, COVID supply crunch, 2020–2024 AI chip demand, CHIPS Act investments). Numbers show closing market caps (billions USD) by year to illustrate the story arc: one firm shoots to the top while a historic giant stumbles.

If this visualization hits you the way it hit me — like, comment your favorite moment, subscribe for more chart races, and share this one. What industry should we race next?
